newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 8.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- President Kim Young-sam announced on Tuesday that an Advisory Committee for Financial Reform would be set up under his leadership for a full-scale reorganisation of the financial sector. This would open the way to mergers and acquistions among financial institutions and the integration of banks, insurance and stock companies.

- President Kim Young-sam said on Tuesday, in reference to nationwide strikes by labor unions "that the Labor Law, having not been changed in the last 43 years, was revised to fit a more developed-nation status" and asked for the cooperation and patience of both management and labor.

- Strikes are spreading to the public sector as well. The Chairman of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, Kwon Young-kil, announced on Tuesday that "labor unions of four broadcast stations and 24 large hospitals had also joined the strike".
